C44988.observed: What was checked: that every job line on a work order offers a way to add a part, including a line that has no parts on it yet. What happened: the work order used had three job lines, and each one showed an "Add Part" button inside its own "Parts" area. None of the three had any parts listed at the time, and the button was still offered on all of them. Both things the test asks for are true.

C44989.observed: What was checked: that pressing "Add Part" opens a new blank row in the right place, with the typing cursor already in the description box. What happened: the new row appeared immediately underneath the "Add Part" button and above the parts already on the line - measured on the page, the button sits higher up, the new row next, and the first existing part below it. The cursor was already sitting in the Description box, so you can start typing straight away without clicking anything.

C44990.observed: What was checked: that the new row shows different things depending on which view the user is in. What happened: in Full View the row offered six boxes - Description, Part number, Qty, Category, Cost and Sell price. In Tech View, checked on the same build, the same row offered only three - Description, Part number and Qty - with no prices anywhere. That is exactly the difference the test expects.

C44991.observed: What was checked: that the small Edit control on a part only appears when you point at the part, and also when you reach it using the keyboard instead of a mouse. What happened: with the mouse elsewhere the control is invisible. Moving the mouse onto the part row makes it appear. Moving the mouse away hides it again. Pressing Tab to move the keyboard onto it also makes it appear, and it was reached with a single Tab press - so someone working without a mouse can still find and use it.

C44992.observed: What was checked: that pressing Edit on a part takes a Full View user to the full part details window rather than to a small inline row. What happened: pressing Edit opened the part details window with the heading "Edit Part Request", and no inline row was opened underneath the part. That is the correct route for a Full View user.
C44992.not_observed: The other half of this test - that a Tech View user gets an inline edit row instead - was not covered here, because this session was in Full View. It is being run separately in a Tech View session.

C44997.observed: What was checked: that if you have already started typing a part on one job line and then press "Add Part" on a different line, the system warns you before throwing your typing away. What happened: with the words "ZZAUTOTEST guard" typed into the first line's row, pressing "Add Part" on the second line brought up a warning headed "Discard this part?", saying "The details you entered will be lost.", offering "Keep Editing" and "Discard Part". Nothing opened on the second line while the warning was on screen, and the typing on the first line was still there. So nothing can be lost by accident.
C44997.not_observed: What each of the two buttons then does is a separate test (C45074) and was not checked here.
